hook: Every connected vertex-transitive graph with a prime-power number of vertices has a Hamiltonian cycle.
summary: A vertex-transitive graph looks the same from every vertex, and the authors show that when its vertex count is a prime power (at least 3), a cycle visiting every vertex exactly once always exists. They extend Witte's 1986 theorem on Cayley digraphs of p-groups. It covers only prime-power orders, so the general question stays open.
title: Hamilton cycles in vertex-transitive graphs of prime-power order
